body:
Seen in run 0442c97d6b8bf128 on task:be36c1d67353660d (step 21). `task peek task:3254586664024306 --notes 1 2 8 9 10 11 12` was refused with just `task peek has no 2`. `board.peek_flags` takes the next word as the note list, and then any further word is an unknown flag.

Other list readers already use one comma form, `3,7,10..12` (`read --lines`, `strategy show note`, `strategy show run`). `task peek --notes` keeps that form, so there is one way to name several items. No space-separated form is added.

- `task peek --notes` accepts `3,7,10..12` (check it already does, and add support if not).
- A bare number after the list is refused with a message that says notes take one list, e.g. `--notes 1,2,8..12`.
- `help task` shows the form in the `task peek` line.

Check: a unit test where `--notes 1 2` is refused with the `1,2` example, and `--notes 1,8..9` returns notes 1, 8 and 9.
title: task peek: note lists like other reads
